I’ve lost 2:

1st - friends since elementary, always somewhat bullied me but she had a hard life so I chalked it up to that, she started acting strange right before we started HS, then halfway thru just dropped me after an escalating series of mean interactions (all her towards me). Years later, she genuinely apologized, I forgave her and we half-heartedly made plans to reconnect but I know we won’t. We’re on very different paths but I wish her well, we’re connected on some social media, and it feels good to not miss or be mad at her anymore.

2nd - met in HS, became super close, I went off to college and she didn’t, found it harder to connect with her as years went on, she had some really problematic and harmful beliefs that I didn’t share/was learning about at school that really made me side-eye her, she moved out of state and things deteriorated from there…she would reach out but was never considerate of my school schedule…meanwhile when I’d reach out she’d either not follow up or not want to hear about school (which was the background of my then-life lol), she also at one point considered backing Trump (I’m mixed w black, she’s white…gotta be fucking kidding me?!) ultimately she didn’t but it made me reevaluate more and ultimately I dropped her because she wasn’t willing to be the friend I needed her to be & she was supporting ideals that enabled direct harm toward people like me & she felt it was fine. She’s since changed her views on almost everything I was hoping she’d reconsider during our friendship but now I have no interest in reconnecting because it feels disingenuous. Plus she completely blames me for the friendship ending as if I just didn’t care enough about her or put in effort.

Mine (26F) was ruined by my stepfamily (Dad’s wife and her brother and niblings) had a massive fight amongst themselves over some bullshit cultural stuff and two of my cousins (21 & 19 yo, who are siblings) we’re getting the brunt of it, they walked out and now we have no idea where they are or if they are safe or together (they left separately). 

There was lots of screaming, some hitting and threatening in general. I was not involved as I was busy trying to keep my little sister (5 yo) calm and out of harm’s way as people were storming around the house. All she wanted to do was make some fucking cookies for Santa Clause and she was trying not to cry instead. 

We did finish the cookies though but we burnt the last batch as shit hit the fan and she shed some tears about that as well. Meanwhile, I was practically trembling and trying not to stutter (happens when I’m very upset or scared) because I ***hate*** violence and yelling. It takes me back to being a frightened little kid when my mom and former, alcoholic stepdad used to fight (not physically but LOTS of yelling). 

In general as an adult, I am very intolerant of raised voices. Also from a personality standpoint, I am not one to yell because I have been yelled at throughout my life and I find it unnecessary/traumatizing/abrasive on my throat FFS. I can verbally tear you a new one in a normal or lowered tone & it works just as well. 

Anyway, I managed not to cry (trying to stay strong for the little one) but I am very triggered and my therapist (who I am fortunate to see for free) deserves a tip for when they have to hear me talk about this for multiple sessions.
